mcqs.question: Which of the following quadrilaterals is defined as having both pairs of opposite sides parallel?
mcqs.explanation: A parallelogram is the quadrilateral in which each pair of opposite sides is parallel. A trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides, a kite has no parallel sides, and an irregular quadrilateral does not satisfy the parallel condition. Hence option C is correct.

mcqs.question: In a rectangle, the diagonals:

options.A: Are equal in length and bisect each other
options.C: Are unequal but bisect each other

mcqs.answer: Are equal in length and bisect each other
mcqs.explanation: A rectangle’s diagonals are congruent (equal in length) and they intersect at their midpoints, thereby bisecting each other. They are not generally perpendicular (that occurs in a square or rhombus). Therefore option A correctly describes the diagonal property of a rectangle.

mcqs.question: Which quadrilateral has all sides equal, opposite sides parallel, and its diagonals are equal in length?
mcqs.explanation: A square satisfies three conditions: all four sides are equal, opposite sides are parallel (making it a parallelogram), and its diagonals are equal in length. A rhombus has equal sides and parallel opposite sides but its diagonals are not equal. A rectangle has equal diagonals but adjacent sides are not necessarily equal. Hence the square uniquely meets all three criteria.

mcqs.learning_point: Use properties to identify an unknown quadrilateral
mcqs.question: A quadrilateral has one pair of opposite sides parallel, the non‑parallel sides are equal in length, and one interior angle is a right angle. Which quadrilateral matches this description?
mcqs.explanation: The description fits an isosceles trapezium (right trapezoid): it has exactly one pair of parallel sides, the two non‑parallel sides are equal (isosceles), and a right angle is present. A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides, a parallelogram has both pairs parallel, and a kite has no parallel sides, so they do not satisfy the given conditions.

mcqs.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, which pair of sides are opposite to each other?
mcqs.explanation: Opposite sides are those that do not share a common vertex. In ABCD, side AB is opposite side CD, while BC is opposite AD. Options A, C, and D describe adjacent sides, not opposite ones.

mcqs.question: Which two interior angles of quadrilateral ABCD are opposite each other?
mcqs.explanation: Opposite angles are those that do not share a common side. In quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A (at vertex A) and ∠C (at vertex C) are opposite. ∠A and ∠B, ∠B and ∠C, and ∠C and ∠D are adjacent pairs.

mcqs.question: Quadrilateral P has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, while quadrilateral Q has only one pair of opposite sides parallel. Which statement is true?

options.A: P is necessarily a rectangle, and Q is necessarily a kite.
options.B: P can be a parallelogram, and Q can be a trapezium.
options.C: Both P and Q must be rhombuses.
options.D: P must be a square, and Q must be a rectangle.

mcqs.answer: P can be a parallelogram, and Q can be a trapezium.
mcqs.explanation: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel is a parallelogram (which includes rectangles, squares, rhombuses as special cases). A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel is a trapezium (trapezoid). Therefore option B correctly captures the possible classifications. The other options incorrectly restrict the shapes.

mcqs.question: A quadrilateral has diagonals that are equal in length, bisect each other, and intersect at right angles. Which quadrilateral must it be?
mcqs.explanation: For a quadrilateral to have diagonals that are (i) equal, (ii) bisect each other, and (iii) intersect at 90°, it must satisfy the properties of both a rectangle (equal, bisecting diagonals) and a rhombus (perpendicular bisecting diagonals). The only shape that fulfills both sets of properties simultaneously is a square. Hence option C is the correct answer.
